title: Sum, Difference and Double-Angle Formulas
seo_title: Sum and Difference Formulas Worksheet with Double-Angle Formulas | 100 Questions
standard_text: Prove the addition and subtraction formulas for sine, cosine, and tangent and use them to solve problems.
meta_desc: Free precalculus worksheet on the sum, difference and double-angle formulas: exact values like sin 75°, recognizing expansions, given values and projectile range. 100 questions.
key_big: sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B
key_sub: cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B. sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ.
body_html:
How it works

  • sin(A ± B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B
  • cos(A ± B) = cos A cos B ∓ sin A sin B (the sign flips)
  • tan(A ± B) = (tan A ± tan B) / (1 ∓ tan A tan B)
  • Double angle: sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ, cos 2θ = cos² θ − sin² θ = 2 cos² θ − 1 = 1 − 2 sin² θ.
  • To find an exact value like sin 75°, write the angle as a sum or difference of special angles: 75° = 45° + 30°.
Example

Find sin 75°.

sin(45° + 30°) = sin 45° cos 30° + cos 45° sin 30°

= √22 · √32 + √22 · 12

Answer: √6 + √24

Example

If sin θ = 35 and θ is in Quadrant II, find sin 2θ.

cos θ = −45

sin 2θ = 2(35)(−45)

Answer: −2425

Common mistakes

  • Writing sin(A + B) = sin A + sin B. It is not true in general.
  • Keeping the same sign in the cosine formula. cos(A + B) has a minus sign.
  • Writing sin 2θ = 2 sin θ. Use 2 sin θ cos θ.
  • Forgetting to find cos θ with the correct sign before using a formula.

faq.q: What is the sum formula for sine?
faq.a: sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B, and sin(A − B) = sin A cos B − cos A sin B.

faq.q: Why does the sign change in the cosine formula?
faq.a: cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B. The sign in the middle is the opposite of the sign between the angles.

faq.q: How do you find sin 15° exactly?
faq.a: Write 15° = 45° − 30° and use sin(A − B). The result is (√6 − √2)/4.
sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ and cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ, which also equals 2cos²θ − 1 or 1 − 2sin²θ.
